verdict: Your project bullets have good raw material, but most experience bullets describe duties instead of actions and results.

rewrites.original: Responsible for preparing weekly stock reports in Excel.
rewrites.improved: Prepared weekly stock reports in Excel (pivot tables, VLOOKUP) for the supply chain team, covering [number of SKUs/stores] and used in [weekly planning meetings].
rewrites.why: Starts with an action verb, names the tools you already list and shows scope. Fill in the brackets only with true details; otherwise remove them.

rewrites.original: Helped the team with data entry and cleaning of supplier data.
rewrites.improved: Cleaned and validated supplier data for [number] suppliers, fixing [type of errors, e.g. duplicates and missing codes] to improve report accuracy.
rewrites.why: 'Helped with' hides your contribution. 'Cleaned and validated' matches the job posting's wording — use it only if it describes what you did.

rewrites.original: Built a forecasting model that was better than the old method.
rewrites.improved: Built a [model type] demand forecasting model in Python that reduced forecast error (MAPE) from [X%] to [Y%] compared with the previous method.
rewrites.why: Turns a vague claim into a measurable result. Use the real metric and values from your project; if you did not measure them, describe the method instead.

rewrites.original: Made a dashboard about Istanbul traffic data.
rewrites.improved: Built a [tool, e.g. Power BI] dashboard visualising [data source] Istanbul traffic data to show [key insight, e.g. peak congestion hours by district].
rewrites.why: Names the tool, the data and the insight — this is what the BI requirement asks for. Only name a tool you actually used.

rewrites.original: Worked at the cash register and helped customers.
rewrites.improved: Handled daily cash transactions and customer requests in a busy bookstore, serving around [N] customers per shift.
rewrites.why: Shorter and more concrete; keep it brief because it is less relevant to a data role.

strengths.point: Your volunteering bullet already shows a concrete result.
strengths.evidence: Member of the university Data Science Club, organized 2 workshops for 40+ students.

strengths.point: The project bullet gives scope with real numbers.
strengths.evidence: Used Python (pandas) to analyse 2 years of daily sales data from 12 stores.

issues.evidence: Responsible for preparing weekly stock reports in Excel.
issues.problem: 'Responsible for' describes a duty, not what you achieved.
issues.fix: Start each bullet with an action verb (Prepared, Built, Analysed, Automated) and end with a result or scope.

issues.evidence: Built a forecasting model that was better than the old method.
issues.problem: 'Better' is unmeasured, so the strongest project ends on a weak note.
issues.fix: Add the measured improvement or describe the method, as in the suggested rewrite.

issues.evidence: Attended meetings with the planning team.
issues.fix: Remove it, or replace it with a concrete contribution you made.
